title: CloudFront 4xx/5xx Error Rate Spike

compliance.assurance_rationale: Saved search evidence for SI-4 when alert outputs are archived.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay or inject sample `aws:cloudfront:accesslogs` events matching `sc_status>=400` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.155 search returns >=1 row and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudfront:accesslogs` traffic without `sc_status>=400` markers. Confirm the search returns zero rows and alert does not fire.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with permission to search `index=aws`.
• Install and configure: Splunk Add-on for AWS (`Splunk_TA_aws`, Splunkbase 1876).
• Ensure `aws:cloudfront:accesslogs` events are flowing (prerequisite UC: 4.1.78 when applicable).
• Map `aws` and field extractions per `docs/guides/aws.md`, `docs/guides/azure.md`, or `docs/guides/gcp.md` as appropriate.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable cloudfront integration in AWS and forward findings/logs via `Splunk_TA_aws` into `index=aws` with `sourcetype=aws:cloudfront:accesslogs`. Validate field extractions before alerting.
Expected sourcetype: `aws:cloudfront:accesslogs`. Validate with:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudfront:accesslogs" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudfront:accesslogs" sc_status>=400
| table _time cs_host sc_status cs_uri_stem time_taken
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
The search scopes `aws:cloudfront:accesslogs` in `index=aws` and applies `sc_status>=400` to surface `CloudFront 4xx/5xx Error Rate Spike`. Tune time range and alert threshold to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare result counts to the vendor console (CloudTrail Event history, Azure Activity Log, GCP Logs Explorer, or service-native UI). Spot-check `_time` and actor fields. Confirm CIM acceleration only after TA field mappings are verified.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_155_alert` with appropriate severity. Dashboard: Notable-style table, severity timeline, single-value open finding count..
Failure modes: (1) empty results — verify TA input and index routing; (2) duplicate events — check S3/SQS duplication; (3) missing fields — upgrade `Splunk Add-on for AWS (`Splunk_TA_aws`, Splunkbase 1876)` and review `props.conf` aliases; (4) alert fatigue — add CMDB/allow-list exclusions documented in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch for cloudfront 4xx/5xx error rate spike in your cloud audit logs so the team catches important changes early instead of finding out from auditors or customers.
